Find the sixth exterior angle.

questions.question_text:
Four exterior angles of a convex pentagon are $60^{\circ}$, $70^{\circ}$, $80^{\circ}$ and $100^{\circ}$. The interior angle at the remaining vertex is $(3x+10)^{\circ}$.
Find the value of $x$.

options.why: Treated the expression as the remaining exterior angle and added $10$ instead of subtracting it: $x=(50+10)\div3=20$.
Treated the sum of the four given exterior angles as the unknown interior angle: $3x+10=310$, giving $x=100$.
Found the interior angle $180-50=130^{\circ}$ and reported $130$ as $x$ without solving $3x+10=130$.

questions.solution_text:
$60+70+80+100=310^{\circ}$
Remaining exterior angle $=360-310=50^{\circ}$, exterior angle sum of a polygon.
$3x+10+50=180$, supplementary angles.
$3x+60=180$
$3x=120$
$x=40$
